---
title: Create a continuous aggregate
description: Create a continuous aggregate and make sure you always have the latest aggregated data for your analytical queries
products: [cloud, self_hosted]
keywords: [continuous aggregates, create]
---

import * as C from "@constants";
import { Callout } from "@stainless-api/docs/components";
import { NumberedList, NumberedItem } from "@components/NumberedList";
import SinceRelease from "@components/SinceRelease.astro";
import DoWithAi from "@components/DoWithAi.astro";
import TestPlan from "@components/TestPlan.astro";

A {C.CAGG} stores precomputed rollups so analytical queries avoid rescanning all raw rows. You create the materialized view first, then wire up refresh (policy or manual). You can build on a {C.HYPERTABLE} or stack another {C.CAGG}, and you can define more than one {C.CAGG} per source.

{C.CAGG_CAP}s require a `time_bucket` on the time partitioning column of
the {C.HYPERTABLE}.

By default, views are automatically refreshed. You can adjust this by setting
the [WITH NO DATA](#using-the-with-no-data-option) option. Additionally, the
view can not be a [security barrier view](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/rules-privileges.html).

{C.CAGG_CAP}s use {C.HYPERTABLE}s in the background, which means that they
also use {C.CHUNK} time intervals. By default, the {C.CAGG}'s {C.CHUNK} time
interval is 10 times what the original {C.HYPERTABLE}'s {C.CHUNK} time interval is. For
example, if the original {C.HYPERTABLE}'s {C.CHUNK} time interval is 7 days, the
{C.CAGG}s that are on top of it have a 70 day {C.CHUNK} time
interval.

<DoWithAi />

## Create a {C.CAGG}

In this example, we are using a {C.HYPERTABLE} called `conditions`, and creating a
{C.CAGG} view for daily weather data. The `GROUP BY` clause must
include a `time_bucket` expression which uses time dimension column of the
{C.HYPERTABLE}. Additionally, all functions and their arguments included in
`SELECT`, `GROUP BY`, and `HAVING` clauses must be
[immutable](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/xfunc-volatility.html).

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Create the materialized view">

```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW conditions_summary_daily
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT device,
   time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 day', time) AS bucket,
   AVG(temperature),
   MAX(temperature),
   MIN(temperature)
FROM conditions
GROUP BY device, bucket;
```

To create a {C.CAGG} within a transaction block, use the [WITH NO DATA option](#using-the-with-no-data-option).
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Create a refresh policy">

```sql
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('conditions_summary_daily',
  start_offset => INTERVAL '1 month',
  end_offset => INTERVAL '1 day',
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '1 hour');
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

You can use most {C.PG} aggregate functions in continuous aggregations. To
see what {C.PG} features are supported, check the
[function support table](/learn/continuous-aggregates#function-support).

## Choosing an appropriate bucket interval

{C.CAGG_CAP}s require a `time_bucket` on the time partitioning column of
the {C.HYPERTABLE}. The {C.TIME_BUCKET} allows you to define a time interval, instead of
having to use specific timestamps. For example, you can define a {C.TIME_BUCKET} as
five minutes, or one day.

You can't use [`time_bucket_gapfill`](/reference/timescaledb/hyperfunctions/time_bucket_gapfill/time_bucket_gapfill) directly in a
{C.CAGG}. This is because you need access to previous data to
determine the gapfill content, which isn't yet available when you create the
{C.CAGG}. You can work around this by creating the {C.CAGG}
using [`time_bucket`](/reference/timescaledb/hyperfunctions/time-series-utilities/time_bucket), then querying the {C.CAGG}
using `time_bucket_gapfill`.

## Using the WITH NO DATA option

By default, when you create a view for the first time, it is populated with
data. This is so that the aggregates can be computed across the entire
{C.HYPERTABLE}. If you don't want this to happen, for example if the table is very
large, or if new data is being continuously added, you can control the order in
which the data is refreshed. You can do this by adding a manual refresh with
your {C.CAGG} policy using the `WITH NO DATA` option.

The `WITH NO DATA` option allows the {C.CAGG} to be created
instantly, so you don't have to wait for the data to be aggregated. Data begins
to populate only when the policy begins to run. This means that only data newer
than the `start_offset` time begins to populate the {C.CAGG}. If you
have historical data that is older than the `start_offset` interval, you need to
manually refresh the history up to the current `start_offset` to allow {C.RTAGG}
queries to run efficiently.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Create the view">

```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW cagg_rides_view
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT vendor_id,
time_bucket('1h', pickup_datetime) AS hour,
  count(*) total_rides,
  avg(fare_amount) avg_fare,
  max(trip_distance) as max_trip_distance,
  min(trip_distance) as min_trip_distance
FROM rides
GROUP BY vendor_id, time_bucket('1h', pickup_datetime)
WITH NO DATA;
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Manually refresh the view">
```sql
CALL refresh_continuous_aggregate('cagg_rides_view', NULL, localtimestamp - INTERVAL '1 week');
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Add the policy">
```sql
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('cagg_rides_view',
  start_offset => INTERVAL '1 week',
  end_offset   => INTERVAL '1 hour',
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '30 minutes');
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

## Create a {C.CAGG} with a JOIN

In {C.TIMESCALE_DB} v2.10 and later, with {C.PG} v12 or later, you can
create a {C.CAGG} with a query that also includes a `JOIN`. For
example:

```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW conditions_summary_daily_3
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 day', time) AS bucket,
   AVG(temperature),
   MAX(temperature),
   MIN(temperature),
   name
FROM conditions JOIN devices ON devices.device_id = conditions.device
GROUP BY name, bucket;
```

<Callout variant="note">
For more information about creating a {C.CAGG} with a `JOIN`,
including some additional restrictions, see the
[about {C.CAGG}s section](/learn/continuous-aggregates#continuous-aggregates-with-a-join-clause).
</Callout>

## Query {C.CAGG}s

When you have created a {C.CAGG} and set a refresh policy, you can
query the view with a `SELECT` query. You can only specify a single {C.HYPERTABLE}
in the `FROM` clause. Including more {C.HYPERTABLE}s, tables, views, or subqueries
in your `SELECT` query is not supported. Additionally, make sure that the
{C.HYPERTABLE} you are querying does not have
[row-level-security policies](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html)
enabled.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title={`Query the ${C.CAGG} for a specific device`}>

```sql
SELECT *
  FROM conditions_summary_daily
  WHERE device = 5
  AND bucket >= '2020-01-01'
  AND bucket < '2020-04-01';
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Query for largest metric spreads">

```sql
SELECT *
  FROM conditions_summary_daily
  WHERE max - min > 1800
  AND bucket >= '2020-01-01' AND bucket < '2020-04-01'
  ORDER BY bucket DESC, device DESC LIMIT 20;
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

## Use {C.CAGG}s with mutable functions: experimental

<SinceRelease version="2.20.0" product="tsdb" />

Mutable functions have experimental support in the {C.CAGG} query definition. Mutable functions are enabled
by default. However, if you use them in a materialized query a warning is returned.

When using non-immutable functions you have to ensure these functions produce consistent results across
{C.CAGG} refresh runs. For example, if a function depends on the current time zone you have
to ensure all your {C.CAGG} refreshes run with a consistent setting for this.

## Use {C.CAGG}s with window functions: experimental

<SinceRelease version="2.20.0" product="tsdb" />

Window functions have experimental support in the {C.CAGG} query definition. Window functions are disabled
by default. To enable them, set `timescaledb.enable_cagg_window_functions` to `true`.

<Callout variant="warning">
Support is experimental, there is a risk of data inconsistency. For example, in backfill scenarios, buckets could be missed.
</Callout>

### Create a window function

To use a window function in a {C.CAGG}:

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Create a simple hypertable">
```sql
CREATE TABLE sales (
  time         TIMESTAMPTZ       NOT NULL,
  customer_id  INTEGER           NOT NULL,
  amount       NUMERIC           NOT NULL
) WITH (tsdb.hypertable, tsdb.partition_column = 'time');
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Enable window functions">
As window functions are experimental, you have to set `enable_cagg_window_functions`.

```sql
SET timescaledb.enable_cagg_window_functions TO TRUE;
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Create the ${C.CAGG} with a window function`}>

Window functions must stay within the {C.TIME_BUCKET}. Any query that tries to look beyond the current
{C.TIME_BUCKET} will produce incorrect results around the refresh boundaries.

```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW example_aggregate
  WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
    SELECT
      time_bucket('1d', time),
      customer_id,
      sum(amount) AS amount,
      sum(amount) - LAG(sum(amount),1,NULL) OVER (PARTITION BY time_bucket('1d', time) ORDER BY sum(amount) DESC) AS amount_diff,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY time_bucket('1d', time) ORDER BY sum(amount) DESC)
    FROM sales GROUP BY 1,2;
```

Window functions that partition by time_bucket should be safe even with LAG()/LEAD()
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

### Window function workaround for older versions of {C.TIMESCALE_DB}

For {C.TIMESCALE_DB} v2.19.3 and below, {C.CAGG}s do not support window functions. To work around this:

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Create a simple hypertable">
Create a simple {C.HYPERTABLE} to store a value at a specific time:

```sql
CREATE TABLE example (
  time       TIMESTAMPTZ       NOT NULL,
  value      DOUBLE PRECISION  NOT NULL
) WITH (tsdb.hypertable, tsdb.partition_column = 'time');
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Create a ${C.CAGG} without a window function`}>
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW example_aggregate
  WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
    SELECT
      time_bucket('10 minutes', time) AS bucket,
      first(value, time) AS value
    FROM example GROUP BY bucket;
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Use the lag window function at query time">
This speeds up your query by calculating the aggregation ahead of time. The
delta is calculated at query time.

```sql
SELECT
  bucket,
  value - lag(value, 1) OVER (ORDER BY bucket) AS delta
FROM example_aggregate;
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>
